newsitem.title: UK: UK Treasury softens blow of FIDS abolition.
newsitem.headline: UK Treasury softens blow of FIDS abolition.

text.p: The UK Treasury said it will make provisions in the next Finance Bill to ensure that so-called international headquarters companies can continue to pay dividends out of foreign income without having to pay advance corporation tax.
In a written parliamentary answer, Financial Secretary Dawn Primarolo said the step was intended to maintain Britain's role as a centre for international business.
She also said the government was looking sympathetically at the position of British groups with substantial foreign income.
The brief answer made no mention of possible changes to the definition of international headquarters companies -- now defined as those with more than 80 percent of their shares in foreign hands.

The Financial Times said last Friday the definition might be extended so more highly international British-based companies could continue to pay dividends out of foreign income when Foreign Income Dividends (FIDs) are scrapped in April 1999.
